most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Viral meningoencephalitis, most likely VZV encephalitis without rash (zoster sine herpete); atypical HSV-1 encephalitis is the main alternative
one_line_reason: Acute fever with seizures, encephalopathy and meningism, plus CSF lymphocytic-range pleocytosis (400/uL), high protein and normal glucose, and multifocal non-enhancing FLAIR lesions (temporal, cerebellar, brainstem, periventricular), all point to viral meningoencephalitis. The spread beyond the temporal lobe into the cerebellum and brainstem fits VZV slightly better than classic HSV.
